doc.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Father the preacher-saxophonist and a musical family
summary: Father played saxophone and preached, died when Hanna was seven; siblings sang and played; he banged on the piano until it went to the barn.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well you had certainly, your childhood must have had diverse musical influences. Your father was a preacher.
He played saxophone and he was a preacher as well.
And was there church influence in the musical end of things for you?

I think so. I never went into the church and played piano in a church. That never happened. But my father loved to play saxophone. And so that certainly had to have some effect on me. Although he died when I was seven years old. But my sister played, my mother played, I had a brother who played the trumpet and violin, and I had another brother who played the saxophone and one who sang, actually two who sang. The oldest one sang but singing was never a major thing with him. He became a doctor. And the one next to me loved to sing. He used to like Lawrence Melchior — I don’t know if you know that name, Lawrence Melchior was a great tenor. And he used to come on every Sunday and Lagraus would sing with him. But my situation was a little bit different. The piano was for my sister and my mother, not for me. And I used to bang on it, I was about three years old and used to bang on it. And I kept banging on it. And I kept banging on it. And finally they took it and put it out in the barn.
Oh gee. I thought you were going to say finally they got me some lessons. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
